title: BAKELITE & CHROME STANDARD LAM...
reason: Classic Art Deco chrome and Bakelite standard lamp, a type collectors and decorators chase when sound and rewired; no marks to add value.
findings: Art Deco style floor lamp: slim chrome tube stem with a black sleeve or telescopic joint part way down, a black fluted tapering column (looks like Bakelite or ebonised timber, consistent with the title) with two chrome collars, a polished chrome cup at the foot and a round black base with a beaded metal rim. The bell shaped peach silk shade looks like a later replacement. No maker's mark, label or patent number visible (lamp holder and underside not photographed). The form matches the chrome and Bakelite floor lamps of the 1930s: a web search (19/10/2026) found Carters, an Australian auction house, with sold lots of similar Art Deco chrome and Bakelite floor lamps (166 and 172 cm, round bases with bead trim; the 172 cm one described as circa 1930s with fluted details to the lower part). Prices were not seen and I could not open those pages, for example https://carters.com.au/index.cfm/item/1225374-an-art-deco-chrome-and-black-bakelite-floor-lamp-circa-1930s-a-s . So the title's 'circa 1955' may be too late, but the age cannot be confirmed from the photos. Height of 168 cm in the title is not checkable.
condition: Chrome looks dulled or tarnished in places and the base rim shows wear. Black parts look intact in the photos. Flex and plug look old and would need an electrical check. Shade is probably not original.
rescore_note: Art Deco form standard lamp with a fluted black column (Bakelite or ebonised timber, unconfirmed), tarnished metal collars and a beaded round base, a type made in the 1930s but possibly later as the title says; replacement shade, old flex needing rewiring and no maker's mark, so decorative and saleable but mid band. No sold comparables checked (the Carters page returned a rate limit error).
